g.title: public.campaigns
g.text: One row per campaign send. status tracks the send lifecycle; recipient_count is set at send time and never recomputed. Written by the send route under the service role; admins read and manage under RLS.
Plain-text fallback, sent alongside body_html on every message. Required by CAN-SPAM; not optional.
null = every opted-in client; {"last_visit_months": N} = opted-in clients with a completed appointment in the last N months. The snapshot of what was asked for, not a live filter.
Size of the audience list at send time. Set once, never recomputed — the list is run ONCE and sent to, so preview and send cannot disagree.
draft | sending | sent | failed. text + check, not an enum type.

g.title: public.organizations
g.text: Tenant root. Single row today; every domain table hangs off organization_id for future multi-tenancy.

g.title: public.staff
g.text: Employees. Linked 1:1 to auth.users via user_id. Deactivated (active=false), never deleted. Self-editable personal fields are guarded by trg_guard_staff_self_update.
Whether this person appears as a provider in scheduling (columns, qualification pickers, slot search).

g.title: public.campaign_recipients
g.text: Per-recipient record for a campaign send. resend_message_id links Phase 2 webhook events back to this row. opened_at/clicked_at/unsubscribed_at populated by the Phase 2 webhook. Inserted by the send route on Resend acceptance only — a row here means Resend took the message. Not fully append-only: the three event columns are updated by the webhook, under the service role.
The id Resend returns on acceptance. Stored from phase 1 because phase 2 cannot exist without it: the webhook matches open/click/unsubscribe events to recipients by this value alone.

g.title: public.campaign_recipients:campaign_id->public.campaigns:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (campaign_id) REFERENCES campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.campaign_unsubscribe_tokens
g.text: Single-use tokens for the one-click unsubscribe link in every campaign email. Same pattern as cancellation_tokens: the id IS the token, minted per recipient at send time, claimed by the public unsubscribe route in the same statement that checks used_at is null. The route sets communication_opted_in = false on the token's client and nothing else — no client id is ever accepted from the request.
